title: Retain a paired scalar-admission effect-size gate, then prune the one-shot harness
research_question: Does the GPU-22 sequence-level persisted-scalar candidate have a reproducible same-process effect size large enough to justify a later minimal production trial, without keeping a second scalar-admission authority alive?

experiment.measurement_contract: Derive Boolean output entry counts from the existing packed-CPU fixture family, compare the current per-entry relation_blocks._stored control with the already semantically proved sequence-level candidate, and collect seven paired alternating AB/BA samples after three warmups in one CPython 3.12 process.

same_head_constructor_profile.interpretation: cProfile attribution contains observer overhead and is not additive wall-time evidence.

experiment.result: The sequence-level candidate had the lower paired median in all six bounded Boolean cases. Observed candidate/control ratios ranged from about 0.788 to 0.829 for this scalar-admission microstage. This is sufficient to nominate a later minimal in-place production trial, not to claim constructor-wide or CPU-wide acceleration.

gardening_close.reason: The retained exact-head artifact preserves the decision evidence, so the temporary probe, test mirror, and upload step do not remain as a second live scalar-admission or benchmark surface.

claim_boundary.allowed: A bounded CPython 3.12 same-process microstage result supports nominating one minimal production consolidation trial.

next_narrow_step: If still before 2026-09-29, replace the per-entry _stored dispatch with one in-place sequence-level admission owner inside TypedRelationBlock, delete the old helper rather than retaining both abstractions, preserve exact first-error/canonicalization semantics, and require same-head semantic plus constructor evidence before keeping the production change.
